concepts.title: Inflation
concepts.summary: Prices rise over time.

lesson.title: Prices creep up
sentences: When prices rise, the same money buys less.
If your pay rises slower than prices, you are worse off.

quiz.question: If rent rises 4% and pay rises 2%, are you better off?

concepts.title: Interest rates
concepts.summary: The Bank Rate moves what loans cost.

lesson.title: Rates set the bill
sentences: A fixed rate keeps your payment the same until the deal ends.
When the deal ends, you pay the rate of that year.

quiz.question: Your 2-year fix ends when rates are high. What happens to your payment?

lesson.personal: Your mortgage rate is 4.42% and your fixed deal ends in 165 days.

concepts.title: Emergency fund
concepts.summary: Cash put aside for surprises.

lesson.title: Keep a cushion
sentences: A few months of costs in cash stops a surprise bill turning into debt.
Card debt costs far more than savings earn.

quiz.question: A £500 bill arrives and you have no savings. What is the cheapest way to pay?

lesson.personal: Your cash and savings cover 3.7 months of spending.

concepts.title: Job security
concepts.summary: Jobs are less safe when unemployment rises.

lesson.title: When jobs get scarce
sentences: When unemployment rises, more people lose jobs and new jobs are harder to find.
Savings buy you time to find the right next job.

quiz.question: Unemployment is rising. What helps most?

concepts.title: House prices
concepts.summary: Home values go down as well as up.

lesson.title: Homes can fall in value
sentences: House prices can fall for several years in a row.
You only lose money on a fall if you sell or must sell.

quiz.question: Prices fall 10% and you do not sell. Have you lost cash?

concepts.title: Spreading risk
concepts.summary: Do not put all your eggs in one basket.

lesson.title: Spread your bets
sentences: Shares can fall a lot in one year and recover over several.
People who sell after a crash often miss the recovery.

quiz.question: The market falls 30%. What did long-term investors usually do best by?

concepts.title: Insurance
concepts.summary: Pay a little to avoid a big loss.

lesson.title: Small cost, big cover
sentences: Insurance turns a rare big loss into a small regular cost.
The excess is the part you still pay when you claim.

quiz.question: What is the excess on a policy?

concepts.title: Budgeting
concepts.summary: Know what comes in and what goes out.

lesson.title: Track the bills
sentences: Bills that rise every month add up over a year.
Cutting one regular cost often beats one big saving.

quiz.question: Which saves more over a year: £20 a month or £200 once?

lesson.personal: You spend £38 a month on 2 subscriptions.

concepts.title: Crypto risk
concepts.summary: Crypto can double or halve in a year.

lesson.title: Wild swings
sentences: Crypto prices can rise or fall by more than half in one year.
Only put in money you can afford to lose.

quiz.question: How much should you put in something that can halve in a year?

concepts.title: Compound interest
concepts.summary: Interest earns interest.

lesson.title: Money that grows itself
sentences: Interest added to savings earns interest the next year.
Debt compounds the same way, so it grows if you do not pay it.

quiz.question: £1,000 earns 5% a year. After two years is it more or less than £1,100?

lesson.personal: Your savings of £6,850 earned £86 in interest in the last year.

concepts.title: Pensions
concepts.summary: Money for later, with a boost from your employer.

lesson.title: Future you
sentences: Your employer adds to your pension when you pay in.
Money paid in early has the longest time to grow.

quiz.question: Who adds money to a workplace pension?

concepts.title: Scams
concepts.summary: If it sounds too good to be true, it is.

lesson.title: Stop and check

chart.title: Bank Rate (real returns are near this)

sentences: Your bank will never ask you to move money to a safe account.
Returns far above normal rates are a warning sign.

quiz.question: A caller says your account is at risk and asks you to move money. What do you do?
options: Hang up and call the bank

concepts.title: Subscriptions
concepts.summary: Small monthly costs add up.

lesson.title: The quiet drain
sentences: A £10 monthly subscription costs £120 a year.
Prices of subscriptions often rise faster than other prices, so check them each year.

quiz.question: You pay £8 a month for an app you never open. What does it cost in a year?

concepts.title: Energy bills
concepts.summary: A fixed energy price trades a small extra cost for no surprises.

lesson.title: Fix or float
sentences: A fixed energy deal keeps your price the same even when the market jumps.
A fix often costs a little more than the standard price when prices are calm.

quiz.question: Energy prices are about to jump 50%. Which deal protects you?

concepts.title: Debt
concepts.summary: Borrowing costs money every month.

lesson.title: The cost of borrowing
sentences: Card debt charges interest far above the Bank Rate.
Paying off expensive debt first saves the most.

quiz.question: You have a card at 20% and savings at 4%. What should you pay off first?

concepts.title: Depreciation
concepts.summary: Cars lose value every year you own them.

lesson.title: Cars lose value
sentences: A car loses value each year, and you also pay to run it.
The cheapest car is often the one you already own.

quiz.question: You buy a car for £10,000. What is it worth after five years?

concepts.title: Running a car
concepts.summary: Fuel, insurance and repairs cost more than the car.

lesson.title: The real cost of a car
sentences: Fuel, insurance, tax and repairs often cost more each year than the car loses in value.
Shopping around at renewal can cut insurance by a lot.

quiz.question: Your car insurance renews 30% higher. What should you do first?

concepts.title: Household costs
concepts.summary: A partner or a child changes the budget.

lesson.title: More people, more costs
sentences: A child adds hundreds of pounds a month to household costs.
Two incomes in one home can share rent and bills.

quiz.question: Which usually lowers the cost per person of a home?

concepts.title: Childcare
concepts.summary: Childcare can cost as much as rent.

lesson.title: The cost of care
sentences: Full-time nursery can cost more than a monthly rent.
Free hours and tax-free childcare cut the bill, but you must apply.

quiz.question: Who must apply for tax-free childcare?

concepts.title: Inheritance
concepts.summary: Money passed on when someone dies.

lesson.title: What gets passed on
sentences: Most inheritances in the UK are a share of a home.
Paying off expensive debt with a windfall beats spending it.

quiz.question: You inherit £10,000 and owe £3,000 on a card. What is the best first step?
options: Leave it in a current account

concepts.title: Splitting up
concepts.summary: A split divides one home into two.

lesson.title: Two homes cost more
sentences: When a couple splits, two homes cost more than one.
Assets such as homes and pensions are usually shared out.

quiz.question: After a split, what usually happens to housing costs per person?

concepts.title: Health and money
concepts.summary: Being ill can cost you pay.

lesson.title: Health is wealth
sentences: Time off sick can cut your pay if your employer pays only statutory sick pay.
Cheap habits like walking protect both health and money.

quiz.question: Statutory sick pay is usually...

concepts.title: Income protection
concepts.summary: Cover that pays you if you cannot work.

lesson.title: If you cannot work
sentences: Income protection insurance pays part of your salary if illness stops you working.
Savings of a few months do the same job for short gaps.

quiz.question: What does income protection replace?

concepts.title: Skills pay
concepts.summary: New skills can raise your pay.

lesson.title: Invest in yourself
sentences: Skills you learn can raise your pay for the rest of your working life.
A course costs money now and may pay back over many years.

quiz.question: A £1,000 course raises your pay £1,000 a year. When has it paid back?

concepts.title: Student loans
concepts.summary: You repay only when you earn enough.

lesson.title: Not like other debt
sentences: You repay 9% of what you earn above a threshold, not a fixed monthly amount.
Any balance left after the repayment period is written off.

quiz.question: You earn below the threshold. How much do you repay that month?

concepts.title: State pension
concepts.summary: A pension from the state from your mid-60s.

lesson.title: The state's part
sentences: The state pension starts at state pension age and needs years of National Insurance.
It is not enough to live on for most people, so a workplace pension matters.

quiz.question: What do you need to build a full state pension?

concepts.title: Benefits
concepts.summary: Help from the state when income is low.

lesson.title: A safety net
sentences: Universal Credit tops up income for people out of work or on low pay.
The rules and amounts change, so check what you can get each year.

quiz.question: You lose your job. What should you check first?

concepts.title: Tax bands
concepts.summary: Each slice of pay is taxed at its own rate.

lesson.title: How income tax works
sentences: Income tax charges each slice of pay at its own rate, so a raise never lowers take-home pay.
When bands stay frozen and pay rises, more of your pay is taxed at higher rates.

quiz.question: A raise pushes you into the higher band. Is all your pay now taxed at 40%?

concepts.title: Fixed or variable
concepts.summary: A fix trades flexibility for certainty.

lesson.title: Certainty has a price
sentences: A fixed rate stays the same while a variable rate moves with the Bank Rate.
A longer fix protects you from rises but you pay a fee to leave early.

quiz.question: Rates look set to rise. Which deal protects your payment?

concepts.title: Negative equity
concepts.summary: Owing more than your home is worth.

lesson.title: Underwater
sentences: You are in negative equity when your mortgage is bigger than your home's value.
It only costs you if you must sell or remortgage before prices recover.

quiz.question: Your home is worth £180,000 and you owe £200,000. What is your equity?

concepts.title: Renting
concepts.summary: Rents move with local demand.

lesson.title: Rent rises
sentences: Rents in your area can rise faster than your pay.
Moving costs money, so a small rise can be cheaper than moving.

quiz.question: Your rent rises £30 a month and moving costs £900. How many months until moving pays off?

concepts.title: Saving a deposit
concepts.summary: Lenders want part of the price up front.

lesson.title: The deposit hurdle
sentences: A bigger deposit usually gets you a lower mortgage rate.
When house prices rise faster than you save, the deposit gets further away.

quiz.question: A £200,000 home with a 10% deposit needs how much up front?

concepts.title: Own or rent
concepts.summary: Owning builds equity but ties up money.

lesson.title: Own or rent?

chart.title: Homes owned by the people living in them

sentences: Paying a mortgage builds equity, while rent buys only a place to live.
Owning also brings repair bills and moving costs that renters do not pay.

quiz.question: Who pays for a broken boiler in a rented flat?

concepts.title: Remortgaging
concepts.summary: Switch deals before yours ends.

lesson.title: Do not drift to the standard rate
sentences: When a fixed deal ends, lenders move you to a higher standard rate unless you switch.
You can usually lock in a new deal up to six months before the old one ends.

quiz.question: Your fix ends next month and you do nothing. What happens?
options: You move to the standard rate

concepts.title: Real returns
concepts.summary: What savings earn after prices rise.

lesson.title: Beat inflation
sentences: If your savings earn less than inflation, they buy less each year.
The real return is the interest rate minus the inflation rate.

quiz.question: Savings earn 2% and prices rise 5%. What is the real return?

concepts.title: Shopping around
concepts.summary: Loyalty rarely pays.

lesson.title: Loyalty costs
sentences: Banks often pay old customers less than new ones.
Checking your rates once a year can earn you more for little effort.

quiz.question: Your bank pays 1% and a rival pays 4% on £5,000. What is the gap in a year?

concepts.title: Drip feeding
concepts.summary: Investing a little each month smooths the ride.

lesson.title: Little and often
sentences: Investing a fixed amount each month buys more shares when prices are low.
It takes the guesswork out of choosing a good time to invest.

quiz.question: Prices fall and you invest the same £100. Do you buy more or fewer shares?

concepts.title: Bonds
concepts.summary: Lending to the government for a fixed return.

lesson.title: Steady but not risk-free
sentences: A government bond pays a fixed interest rate until it ends.
When rates rise, existing bonds fall in price.

quiz.question: Interest rates rise sharply. What happens to the price of old bonds?

concepts.title: Currency
concepts.summary: The pound buys more or less abroad.

lesson.title: The pound abroad
sentences: A weaker pound makes holidays and imported goods cost more.
Shares in global companies can rise in pounds when the pound falls.

quiz.question: The pound falls against the dollar. A US holiday costs...

concepts.title: Credit cards
concepts.summary: Clear the balance in full to avoid interest.

lesson.title: Pay in full
sentences: If you clear the full balance each month, a credit card charges no interest.
Paying only the minimum can take years and cost more than you borrowed.

quiz.question: You pay only the minimum each month. What happens to the interest you pay?

concepts.title: Opportunity cost
concepts.summary: Every choice gives up another one.

lesson.title: What you give up
sentences: Money you spend today cannot grow for tomorrow.
The true cost of a choice includes the best thing you gave up.

quiz.question: You spend £1,000 instead of investing at 5%. What did you give up in year one?

concepts.title: Pay growth
concepts.summary: Pay rises with the economy, unevenly.

lesson.title: Keeping up
sentences: Typical pay in your area rises most years, but not always faster than prices.
A pay rise below inflation is a pay cut in what your money buys.

quiz.question: Your pay rises 2% and prices rise 5%. Can you buy more or less?

concepts.title: Asking for more
concepts.summary: If you do not ask, the answer is no.

lesson.title: Know your worth
sentences: Knowing the typical pay for your job helps you ask for a fair raise.
A raise early in your career grows with every later raise.

quiz.question: Which helps most when asking for a raise?

concepts.title: Redundancy
concepts.summary: When a job goes, the law sets a minimum payout.

lesson.title: When jobs go
sentences: Statutory redundancy pay depends on your age, pay and years in the job.
Redundancies rise when unemployment rises.

quiz.question: What increases statutory redundancy pay?

concepts.title: Employer risk
concepts.summary: Your employer can go bust.

lesson.title: Do not bet twice
sentences: If your employer goes bust, you can lose your job and unpaid wages.
Holding a lot of your employer's shares doubles that risk.

quiz.question: Why hold few shares in your own employer?
options: Your job already depends on it

concepts.title: Flood risk
concepts.summary: Some homes are far more likely to flood.

lesson.title: Water damage

chart.title: Chance of a flood per year

sentences: A small yearly chance of a flood adds up over the years you own a home.
Insurance and flood defences cut the cost when it happens.

quiz.question: A 1% flood chance each year, over 30 years, is roughly...

concepts.title: Home security
concepts.summary: Simple locks cut burglary risk.

lesson.title: Lock it up
sentences: Burglary rates differ a lot between areas and years.
Good locks can lower both the risk and the insurance price.

quiz.question: Which usually lowers home insurance?

concepts.title: Where you live
concepts.summary: Pay and prices differ by region.

lesson.title: Place matters
sentences: Pay and house prices differ a lot between UK regions.
A higher salary can buy less if local homes cost much more.

quiz.question: London pay is higher. Does that always make London cheaper to live in?

concepts.title: The energy price cap
concepts.summary: A limit on the unit price, not the bill.

lesson.title: Caps are not limits on bills
sentences: The energy price cap limits the price per unit, not your total bill.
If you use more energy, you still pay more.

quiz.question: The price cap falls. Can your bill still rise?

concepts.title: Fuel costs
concepts.summary: Fuel prices swing with oil and the pound.

lesson.title: Pain at the pump
sentences: Fuel prices follow oil prices and the value of the pound.
Driving less is the only sure way to cut a fuel bill.

quiz.question: Which cuts a fuel bill for sure?
